t: You're looking at the statue of Charles II in the Figure Court of the Royal Hospital, Chelsea. It was carved around sixteen eighty to sixteen eighty-two by Grinling Gibbons, an Anglo-Dutch sculptor and wood carver whose work also appears at Windsor Castle, Hampton Court Palace and St Paul's Cathedral. The king founded the Royal Hospital in sixteen eighty-two as a home for retired army veterans, so the statue honours the man who started the place. It is Grade One listed.
